title: Correlation of thyroid hormones with exocrine and endocrine pancreatic function in cystic fibrosis
summary:
Many cystic fibrosis patients develop pancreatic dysfunction at a very early age, resulting in insufficient production of digestive enzymes. In some cases, this occurs at birth. As the disease progresses, the dysfunction often affects hormone production (especially insulin), leading to impaired glucose tolerance and, in some cases, diabetes mellitus in cystic fibrosis. Some cystic fibrosis patients were able to produce digestive enzymes again under highly effective CFTR modulator therapy (a causal therapy class for cystic fibrosis patients), while in others the functional impairment of the pancreas was irreversible. 
Thyroid hormones are important for the developmental maturation of the pancreas. The study will investigate whether the thyroid hormones measured in the blood of newborns can predict the pancreatic function of cystic fibrosis patients. It will also investigate whether current thyroid parameters influence hormone production in the pancreas.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of available thyroid values for Heidelberg CF patients from 1998 to 2025 with regard to the endocrine and exocrine pancreatic function of the patients and the clinical course of the underlying disease.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who were in treatment between 1998 and 2025 and participate in the registry study “Establishment of a biobank and DNA bank with registry for patients with cystic fibrosis” (S-370/2011)
Exclusion criteria:
none
